extraction.name: AI2 Reasoning Challenge (ARC)
extraction.description: A new question set, text corpus, and baselines assembled to encourage AI research in advanced question answering. The ARC question set is partitioned into a Challenge Set and an Easy Set, where the Challenge Set contains only questions answered incorrectly by both a retrieval-based algorithm and a word co-occurence algorithm. The dataset contains only natural, grade-school science questions authored for human tests.
extraction.creator: Peter Clark, Isaac Cowhey, Oren Etzioni, Tushar Khot, Ashish Sabharwal, Carissa Schoenick, Oyvind Tafjord
extraction.citeAs: Clark, P., Cowhey, I., Etzioni, O., Khot, T., Sabharwal, A., Schoenick, C., & Tafjord, O. (2018). Think you have Solved Question Answering? Try ARC, the AI2 Reasoning Challenge. arXiv:1803.05457.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The ARC dataset consists of 7787 science questions drawn from a variety of sources, namely questions authored for use on standardized tests. It includes the publically releasable subset of the Kaggle questions. The ARC Corpus was created by utilizing a major search engine to run a large series of search queries relevant to science, collecting and de-duplicating top documents, and chunking into sentences.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Document analysis, Web Scraping
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Science questions authored for use on standardized tests from various sources (e.g., MCAS, NY Regents, TIMSS, Mercury). Web documents retrieved via search engine queries for the corpus.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: several months of extensive search and investigation
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Partitioned into a Challenge Set (2590 questions) and an Easy Set (5197 questions) based on whether they were answered incorrectly by both a retrieval-based algorithm and a word co-occurrence algorithm.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Filtered for non-diagram, multiple choice questions. For the corpus: documents were de-duplicated, content stripped down to capture just the text, and chunked into sentences.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Challenge questions are defined operationally as those answered incorrectly by both an Information Retrieval (IR) Solver and a Pointwise Mutual Information (PMI) Solver. Questions answered correctly by either are placed in the Easy Set.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Although this only approximates the informal goal of it being a 'hard' question, this definition nevertheless serves as a practical and useful filter, as reflected by the low scores of various baselines on the Challenge Set.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Information Retrieval (IR) Solver, Pointwise Mutual Information (PMI) Solver, Elasticsearch
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Encourages AI research in advanced question answering requiring reasoning and commonsense knowledge, moving beyond retrieval-style tasks where surface-level cues alone are sufficient.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Large portions of standardized tests can be easily solved by simple AI methods (retrieval, statistical correlations), biasing research towards incrementally improving those algorithms rather than exploring larger AI challenges. The Challenge Set addresses this by filtering out questions solvable by simple baselines.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Contains only non-diagram, multiple choice questions. The definition of 'Challenge' questions is an approximation based on two specific solvers. The Mercury source data is restricted to non-commercial research purposes.
